history.dynasty: Chola (present masonry structure); enriched by Pallavas, Vijayanagara rulers and Nayaks
history.summary: One of the largest Shiva temples in India (about 8.1 hectares / 20 acres, though some sources say 33 acres - flag, verify), with nine gopurams and six daily rituals. Shiva is worshipped as Thyagarajaswami in his Somaskanda form with consorts Neelotpalambika and Kamalambika; it is the foremost of the Sapta Vidanga Sthalams, famed for Ajapa Natanam - the 'dance without chanting', a cosmic dance said to occur without sound or effort, enacted whenever Thyagaraja's image is taken out in procession. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam sung by the Nayanars, and the separate Achaleswarar shrine in its prakaram is another Nayanmar-sung shrine. Its Aazhi Ther chariot is the largest of its kind in Asia (~90-96 ft high, ~300 tons, carved wood) and is taken out during the Panguni Brahmotsavam (the Tamil saying 'Tiruvarur Terazhagu' celebrates its grandeur); the Kamalalayam/Kamala Pushkarani tank to the west (~25 acres) is among India's largest temple tanks. Thiruvarur was a great Chola cultural centre, patronised especially by Raja Raja Chola I, and is the birthplace of the Carnatic music Trinity - Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar (who composed Kritis on its deities) and Syama Sastri. Administered by the HR&CE Department of Tamil Nadu. HOURS NOTE: timings conflict across sources (6:00 AM-12:00 PM / 4:00 PM-8:30 PM vs 5:00 AM-12:30 PM / 4:00 PM-9:00 PM) - verify on the day.

name: Thyagaraja Temple
town_description: Town and district headquarters in the Cauvery delta; historic Chola cultural centre and birthplace of the Carnatic music Trinity (Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri).

travel.road: Well connected by road to Chennai, Trichy, Madurai and Nagapattinam
